## Application: Estimation of Price Elasticity * Understanding price elasticity is crucial for economic analysis and business decisions - It influences strategies, pricing, and market dynamics * Traditional causal methods rely on structured data, limiting their applicability * Utilizing unstructured data enhances decision-making * Sources like images and text contain valuable insights - Contain rich hidden information about unobserved confounding variables ## Double Machine Learning #### Partially linear regression model (PLR) $$ \begin{align*} &Y = D \theta_0 + g_0(X) + \varepsilon, & &\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon| P,X] = 0, \\ &D = m_0(X) + V, & &\mathbb{E}[V | X] = 0, \end{align*} $$ with :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - Outcome $Y$, e.g. Demand $\ln (Q)$ - Treatment variable $D$, e.g. Price $\ln (P)$ - Additional product features $X = (X_1, \dots)$ - Stochastic errors $\varepsilon$ and $V$ ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](figures/DAG_001.png) ::: :::: $\Rightarrow$ The causal parameter $\theta_0$ can be interpreted as price elasticity of demand! ## Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML) #### Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML) - Use machine learning methods to fit $$ \begin{align*} l_0(X)&:=\mathbb{E}[Y||X]\\ m_0(X)&:=\mathbb{E}[D|X] \end{align*} $$ - Construct the orthogonalized score (either cross-fitting or split the sample) for a fitted nuisance learner $\hat{\eta}_0:=(\hat{l}_0, \hat{m}_0)$ $$ \psi(W,\theta,\hat{\eta}_0) := \Big(Y - \hat{l}_0(X) - \theta\big(D-\hat{m}_0(X)\big)\Big)\Big(D-\hat{m}_0(X)\Big) $$ - Compute the estimate as the solution of $$ 0 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \psi(W,\hat{\theta}_0,\hat{\eta}_0) $$ ## Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML)
- Assumptions for the nuisance elements (see @dml2018) $\lVert \hat{m}_0 - m_0 \rVert_{P,2} \times \big( \lVert \hat{m}_0 - m_0 \rVert_{P,2} + \lVert \hat{\ell}_0 - \ell_0\rVert _{P,2}\big) \le \delta_N N^{-1/2}$ - Under some regularity conditions the estimator $\hat{\theta}_0$ concentrates in $1/\sqrt{n}$-neighborhood of $\theta_0$ and $$ \sqrt{n}(\hat{\theta}_0 - \theta_0) \to \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2) $$ . . . $\Rightarrow$ simple approach to control for product features, *if they can be used for ML models!* ## Application - A presumably very important feature to consider might be product quality. How to determine product quality? Maybe use average rating, number of reviews, etc.

$\lVert \hat{m}_0 - \ln(P) \rVert_{P,2} \le \lVert \hat{m}_0 - m_0 \rVert_{P,2} + \sigma_V$ # Application ## Amazon Toys Dataset - Public Data from the Amazon sales platform from category toys and games for subcategories vehicles, cars and trucks. - Using the Sales Rank as a proxy for quantities, as shown in @bajari2023hedonic. | Variable | Description | | -------- | ------- | | Sales Rank | Sales rank as weighted mean for the last 30 days | | Price | Price as weighted mean for the last 30 days | | Text | Combination of Title, Category, Description, etc. | | Image | First Image of the product | ## Amazon Toys Dataset :::: {.columns .my-table} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Continous Variables** * Reviews: Rating * Reviews: Review Count * New Offer Count: Current * Count of retrieved live offers: New, FBA * Count of retrieved live offers: New, FBM ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Categorical Variables** * Lightning Deals: Upcoming Deal * Buy Box: Is FBA ::: :::: Scatterplots with OLS Regression of Tabular Variables and $\ln(Q)$ ![](figures/tab_pairplot.png) ## Amazon Toys Dataset #### Data Examples :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Kinsmart Set of 4 McLaren 720s Toy | ... ![](figures/img0.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Pixar Cars Mack Uncle Lightning... ![](figures/img1.png) ::: :::: ## Baseline :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} * Baseline estimate with tabular covariates, OLS model for regression - $\ln(Q) = \theta_0 \ln(P) + \beta^T X + \epsilon$ - $R^2 = 0.330$ | 2.5 % | $\theta$ | 97.5 % | | -------- | ------- | ------- | | -0.072 | -0.046 | -0.019 | ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![Centered logarithmic negative sales rank over centered logarithmic price as binned plot](figures/baseline_binned_plot.png) ::: :::: ## Baseline :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} * Estimate with tabular data as covariates $X$ in $\texttt{DoubleMLPLR}$ model with $\texttt{RandomForest}$ regressors - $l_0(X) := \mathbb{E}[\ln(Q)|X]$ - $R^2_{l_0} = 0.5986$ - $m_0(X) := \mathbb{E}[\ln(P)|X]$ - $R^2_{m_0} = 0.1884$ | 2.5 % | $\theta$ | 97.5 % | | -------- | ------- | ------- | | -0.132 | -0.1098 | -0.080 | ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![Residualised logarithmic negative sales rank over residualised logarithmic price as binned plot](figures/baseline_dmlplr.png) ::: :::: ## Deep Learning Models * In this study, a variety of input data combinations were used to train $\texttt{DoubleMLPLRDeep}$ models [^top]: | Key | Used Confounders | | -------- | ------- | | $\texttt{img}$ | $X = (X_{img})$ | | $\texttt{imgtab}$ | $X = (X_{img}, X_{tab})$ | | $\texttt{txtimg}$ | $X = (X_{txt}, X_{img})$ | | $\texttt{txt}$ | $X = (X_{txt})$ | | $\texttt{txttab}$ | $X = (X_{txt}, X_{tab})$ | | $\texttt{txtimgtab}$ | $X = (X_{txt}, X_{img}, X_{tab})$ | . . . $\Rightarrow$ The aim is to emphasize the benefits of utilizing unstructured data. [^top]: Subsequently, the top 5 performing instances for each combination were evaluated based on the minimum RMSE score of the validation data. ## Deep Learning Models: RMSE-Scores :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - Combined RMSE Score (Training) ![](figures/train_comb_loss_mod.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - Combined RMSE Score (Validation) ![](figures/val_comb_loss_mod.png) ::: :::: ## Deep Learning Models: $R^2$-Scores :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - $R^2$ of log(Quantity) on Validation Set ![](figures/R2_ml_l_mod.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - $R^2$ of log(Price) on Validation Set ![](figures/R2_ml_m_mod.png) ::: :::: ## (First) Results :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} * Using different combinations of tabular, image and text data we obtain the following estimates ![](figures/theta_ln_p.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![Continous Estimates from $\texttt{DoubleMLPLR}$ on Validation Set during the Training Process](figures/cont_dml_sub.png) ::: :::: ## Comparison to Baseline Estimates | Model | Covariates | $R^2_{l_0}$ |$R^2_{m_0}$ | $\hat{\theta}_0$ | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $\texttt{OLS}$ | $X=X_{tab}$ | $0.3300$ | - | $-0.0455$ | | $\texttt{DoubleMLPLR}$ | $X=X_{tab}$ | $0.5986$ | $0.1884$ | $-0.1098$ | | $\texttt{DoubleMLPLRDeep}$[^1] | $X=(X_{tab}, X_{txt}, X_{img})$ | $0.5990$ | $0.6765$ | $-0.2794$|
